findings.summary: Code snippet appears without the idea being stated first, and the ADL code block comes before its explanation is complete.
findings.fix: State the one-line idea (alias shortens names; nested namespace definition is C++17) before the code block.

findings.summary: Bullet holds two ideas: reopening across files and extending.
findings.evidence: Can be reopened across files and extended
findings.fix: Keep one idea: 'A namespace can be reopened in any file to add names'.

findings.summary: Bullet holds two ideas: the leak problem and the scope limit are combined with a misplaced term set; also the 'Remember' mixes ADL and using advice.
findings.evidence: ADL only applies to unqualified calls. Prefer using std::cout; over using namespace std;.
findings.fix: Split into two bullets, or keep the Remember to a single point per page topic.

findings.summary: Bullet crams two ideas: internal-linkage replacement of static and the exceptions where static is still needed.
findings.evidence:
Replaces file-scope static on variables and functions
static is still needed for class members and function-local statics
findings.fix: Keep as separate bullets but label the second as an exception; also state the idea 'each TU gets its own copy' before the two-file code.

findings.summary: Two-file code example is followed by an unmarked prose line, and the 'Why No ODR Clash' section shows code with only a trailing sentence as explanation.
findings.fix: Render the result as a small table or label (a.cpp counter | b.cpp counter | separate) and state the claim before the code.

findings.summary: Bullet holds two ideas: forward declaration via known type, and plain enum exception in a separate line with code syntax inline.
findings.evidence:
Known underlying type allows forward declaration
A plain enum can too, if its type is fixed: enum Old : int;
findings.fix: Move the plain-enum exception to its own labelled bullet or drop it.

findings.summary: Interview Point poses questions with answers inline, and the 'Match the type' note mixes a rule with a bare-declaration claim that reads ambiguously.
findings.evidence: Bare enum class Status; means int. If the definition says : uint8_t, repeat it.
findings.fix: Rewrite as one rule: 'A forward declaration must repeat the same underlying type as the definition (default int)'.

findings.summary: Code is shown before its idea is stated, and the getline/token bullet holds two ideas.
findings.evidence: Lines: while (std::getline(in, line)); tokens: while (in >> x)
findings.fix: Split into two bullets (lines / tokens) and put the one-line idea before the cpp block.

findings.summary: Writing code appears before the explanation of what the flag does, and the mistakes section lists bare phrases without the why.
findings.evidence:
while (!in.eof()) can run one extra time
Skipping the open check
std::endl in hot loops
findings.fix: Give each mistake a short consequence, e.g. 'Skipping the open check: a failed open is silent'.

findings.summary: A single bullet packs several ideas about errors and exceptions, making the failure rules hard to skim.
findings.evidence: Failure throws fs::filesystem_error; a range-for ++ can throw even after passing ec
findings.fix: Split into: 'Default overloads throw fs::filesystem_error', 'Pass std::error_code last to avoid throwing', 'Iterator ++ in a range-for can still throw'.

findings.summary: Code example precedes the statement of what it demonstrates, and the Remember warning bundles two ideas.
findings.evidence: fs::path("data") / "/abs" is "/abs", not data/abs. It replaces the whole path, so never append untrusted components.
findings.fix: Split into the rule (absolute right side replaces the path) and the safety advice.

findings.summary: Cheat sheet uses inconsistent terms for the same thing: 'File-local helper' uses unnamed namespace on page 2 but 'static' is dropped without noting the class-member exception, and the enum row is prose rather than a table.
findings.fix: Format the enum class section as a Want | Write table like the others.

findings.summary: The fs::path printing quiz tests a fact that no earlier page teaches.
findings.evidence: "It prints \"/abs/a.txt\" with the double quotes, because operator<< on fs::path uses std::quoted" and "Use p.string() for unquoted text" appear only on the quiz page. Page 5 never mentions that streaming an fs::path quotes it, or that .string() exists.
findings.fix: Add a bullet on page 5, section 1, saying that operator<< on an fs::path prints it in double quotes and that p.string() gives plain text. Or replace the quiz item with one built from taught material, such as the `fs::path("data") / "/abs"` case.

findings.summary: Quiz code appears after its answer in some items, so the learner sees the solution before the question, and the page uses a different heading style from earlier pages.
findings.evidence:
A file ends with a newline. What goes wrong here?
eof() turns true only after a read hits end of file ... while (!in.eof()) {
findings.fix: Place the code immediately after each question and before its answer.
